subject: Traffic canopy & token-slice intake for Comet Labs Dedicated pilot
messages:
From: Ethan Walker <ethan.walker@cometlabs.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Suresh <priya@cometlabs.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pilot — workload snapshot and sample data

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this. We're getting the Comet Labs pilot over the line and want to scope Dedicated capacity ahead of the procurement window. Attached is a small sample of production traces (comet_workload_sample.csv) and a quick diagram of desired SLAs (comet_qos_diagram.png). High level:

- Steady-state traffic: ~80–130 qps (API calls) during business hours (PST).
- Average concurrent active sessions: 6–10 (user-facing chat sessions).
- Burst scenarios: two 20–30 minute bursts per weekday; observed peaks ~380–420 qps during campaign runs.
- Prompt size (tokens): median ~110, 95th ~320.
- Generation length (tokens): median ~320, 95th ~900.
- Typical request = prompt + expected continuation; many flows use streaming for partial responses.

Open questions for us: what conservative fleet sizing would Redwood recommend for an initial Dedicated commit that meets p95 latency <= 700ms and supports the observed bursts while keeping cost predictable? We're also interested in suggestions for session pooling / KV-cache heuristics.

Can you review the CSV and suggest the minimal reserved footprint plus recommended autoscale headroom? We'd like a short call this week if needed.

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan J. Walker
Head of Infrastructure, Comet Labs
ethan.walker@cometlabs.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: comet_workload_sample.csv, comet_qos_diagram.png

From: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pilot — workload snapshot and sample data

Hi Ethan — thanks, the sample and diagram are helpful. Quick clarifying questions before we size:

1) Burst profile: are the 20–30 minute bursts single contiguous windows or repeated micro-bursts inside them?
2) How sensitive is Comet to cold-start tail latency vs. cost? (i.e., would you accept slightly higher p99 if p95 is guaranteed?)
3) Are responses typically generated in streaming mode for the entire session, or only for long-form outputs?
4) Do you expect multi-turn context to exceed 8k tokens for the pilot?

Initial things we'll do after answers:
- Run a quick traffic replay on our sandbox using the CSV to estimate KV cache hit rate and GPU occupancy.
- Surface a conservative reserved footprint plus autoscale plan — we'll include recommended instance SKUs and suggested quantization profile.

I attached a short "sizing intake" workbook (sizing_intake_template.xlsx) to make answering the matrix quick. If you can return the filled fields by EOD tomorrow we can aim to deliver a concrete commit recommendation and cost estimate by Friday.

Proposed 30-min slot: Thu 6/30 9:30–10:00am PT — works for you?

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: sizing_intake_template.xlsx

From: Ethan Walker <ethan.walker@cometlabs.ai>

On Tue, Jun 29, 2027 at 11:02 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Hi Ethan — thanks, the sample and diagram are helpful. Quick clarifying questions before we size:
>
> 1) Burst profile: are the 20–30 minute bursts single contiguous windows or repeated micro-bursts inside them?

Good questions — answers below and I've attached an updated CSV with annotated burst windows (comet_workload_sample.csv v2).

1) The long bursts are usually composed of micro-bursts. In a 25-minute campaign window we'll see ~6 peaks (30–90s) with short fallbacks in between. Overall the burst looks like a jagged skyline rather than one flat peak.
2) Priority order: p95 latency target (<= 700ms) is most important. p99 can be higher; tolerable up to ~2.5s for edge cases.
3) Streaming is enabled for ~40% of flows (mostly for long-form summaries and multi-part outputs). For the rest we expect a single response payload.
4) Multi-turn is usually bounded; context almost always < 6k tokens for pilot.

Additional notes:
- We have strict data residency needs (US only) for some tenants but pilot covers US region.
- We'll enable application-level caching for deterministic paraphrase requests but want Redwood-level KV cache to handle LLM context reuse where appropriate.

Call: Thu 6/30 9:30am PT works for Priya and me.

Thanks — Ethan
Ethan J. Walker
Head of Infrastructure, Comet Labs

Attachment: comet_workload_sample_v2.csv

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Walker <ethan.walker@cometlabs.ai>, Priya Suresh <priya@cometlabs.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 14:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pilot — workload snapshot and sample data

Folks — quick sizing sketch after reviewing the CSV and annotations. This is a conservative starting point to meet p95 <= 700ms and absorb micro-bursts without frequent queuing.

Summary recommendation (initial reserved commit):
- Baseline reserved: 6x A100-40GB (or 6x equivalent 80GB-chopped VMs)
- Autoscale / burst headroom: allow scaling to 10 nodes for sustained campaigns (~400–420 qps observed)
- Runtime config: enable continuous batching with target batch window 10–20ms, prefix KV caching for session hot keys, and a 4-bit quant profile for the main model to reduce occupancy (measure BLEU/regression risk during pilot).
- Routing: prefer p95-latency routing to US-west nodes; keep a cost-fallback variant in a separate pool for non-critical traffic.

Rationale: the model's memory footprint + average token lengths imply ~7–9 concurrent requests per GPU at median prompt/resp sizes; 6 reserved GPUs give steady-state headroom while autoscale handles the jagged burst skyline. We can refine after a 24-hour traffic replay in our sandbox — that will give a more accurate occupancy curve.

Next steps / asks:
- Soojin: schedule the replay run for Thu afternoon and grant access to the sandbox S3 bucket with the sample traces.
- Marissa: prep a short cost delta sheet comparing 6-reserved vs 8-reserved and the autoscale-to-12 tail. Add monthly TCO (reservation + network egress).
- Ethan/Priya: confirm if streaming flows must be prioritized; if yes we'll reserve 2 GPUs optimized for low-latency streaming.

I'll draft a 1-page mutual action plan and drop it in the HubSpot link (see related links).

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
